title: The Ramp-Up Tax Every Business Pays Before Its Busiest Quarter
linkedin:
Your gross margin just dipped, right before your busiest quarter. Before you blame pricing or costs, check the calendar.

If you have hired ahead of a seasonal peak this spring, this is probably the ramp-up tax, not a blowout.

New starters cost a full wage from day one. Their output does not reach the same level for four to twelve weeks, depending on the role. During that stretch, the P&L shows a straight line of extra cost against a curve of rising output, and the two do not meet for a while.

There is a second cost that rarely gets its own line item. Someone has to train the new hire, and it is usually your most capable person. While they are showing someone else how the job works, their own output softens too. Two people's productivity dips for the price of training one.

The mistake we see most often is reading this month's margin against last month's and concluding something has broken. The better read is the trend within the ramp itself. If labour cost against output is improving week on week, it is on schedule. If it is still flat past eight to ten weeks, that is a different conversation.

The businesses that handle this well expect the dip before it arrives and build it into the plan, so a softer September or October margin reads as on track rather than as a warning sign.

If you're an East Coast business owner staffing up for your busiest quarter, whether that's a Christmas trading peak, a spring construction push, or a seasonal surge in bookings, you've probably noticed your margin dip a little in the weeks before things get busy.

That dip is normal. New team members cost a full wage from the day they start, but it takes several weeks for their output to catch up. On top of that, your most experienced staff usually spend part of that time training the new starters, which softens their own numbers too. Put together, it's a predictable and temporary squeeze on margin, not a sign that pricing or costs have gone wrong.

The businesses that handle this best build the dip into their planning ahead of time, so a quieter month before the peak reads as expected rather than alarming. If you're gearing up for spring or the Christmas trading season and want a clearer read on whether your numbers are tracking to plan, this is exactly the kind of pattern we help Brisbane and East Coast business owners make sense of.
